meta.title: BeKavod — home care watch for older parents. No cloud.
meta.desc: A local video and alert system for looking after an elderly relative. The footage never leaves the house. No cloud, no subscription.
hero.kicker: Everything is computed at home · no footage goes to the cloud
hero.h1: He stays home. And you get your own life back.
hero.tick1: Went out the gate. Your phone knows four seconds later.
hero.tick2: Breakfast, twenty minutes. As usual — no alert.
hero.tick3: Afternoon rest longer than usual. Noted. Nobody was woken.
hero.tick4: Went to bed. Overnight the system watches for him getting up.

hero.credit: My grandfather and me. Yavne, August 2026
hero.alt: A grandson holding his grandfather's hand in the yard at sunset
why.lead:
I brought my grandfather to Israel.
        A year later I stopped having a life of my own.
why.p1: He kept leaving the house. I would walk out of work to go find him — and lost the job. I stopped going away for weekends. I slept with one ear open: night is the dangerous part.
why.p2: Nobody says this out loud: caring for someone you love is hard. Loving them does not make it lighter.
why.quote: I did not want to put my grandfather in a care home. I did not want to lose my own life either.
why.p3: So I built a system. Not to watch him — to stop standing guard. He reaches the gate, my phone wakes me in four seconds. Nothing happens, nobody bothers me.
why.p4: He lives at home. I work, I see people, and I sleep.
why.alt: An elderly man smiling in the yard at sunset
card.label: What I am to him
card.note: property and medical · I act on his behalf and in his interest
how.title: How it works
how.sub: You are not watching. It is.
n1.h: The house notices before you do
n1.p1: The eyes are cameras. They cover the places a person leaves from: the gate, the front door, the yard.
n1.p2: The ears are sensors. They cover the places a camera must never go: bathroom, bedroom. A sensor records nothing — it senses movement, breathing and falls.
n1.altSen: A sensor on a room wall
n2.h: It catches what you would miss
n2.p1: What time he went to bed and how often he got up at night. When he ate. Whether he took his medicine. How many times he made it to the bathroom. The system counts all of it by itself, every day, quietly.
n2.p2: On any single day the numbers mean nothing. Over a month they show that someone is getting worse — earlier than you would notice. And you do not have to sit beside him to know it.
n2.canvas: A neural network diagram: nodes joined by lines with pulses travelling along them
n3.p1: A fall in the bathroom. The gate opened at three in the morning. No sign of him by breakfast. These are the cases the whole thing was built for — the rest of the time it stays quiet.
n3.p2: The phone rings loud — like an alarm clock, not like a notification — even on silent. The screen shows what, where and when straight away. Whether to drive over or call is your call. But you hear it first.
n3.alt: Hands holding a phone with alert and message icons around it
n4.c1s: Not the cloud, not us, not the camera maker. There is simply nowhere to send it.
n4.c2s: Your own yard is free to look at. Always.
n4.c3s: A connection is only needed to reach you. Watching and counting happen on the box.
n4.c4s: Switch the box off and nothing is left anywhere.
n4.h: It all stays inside this box
n4.p: It sits on your shelf and fits in one hand. Cameras and sensors talk only to it; it talks only to your phone. That is not a clause in a contract — it is how the system is built: there is no route out.
n4.alt: A small black box of the system on a table
c.h: Write — you get me, not a desk
c.lead: There is no call centre here. On the other side is the same person who built this for his own grandfather.
c.s1e: I will ask about the house and about what worries you most.
c.s2e: Free. Where the gate is, where the bed is, where a camera will never go.
c.s3b: I install it in a day
c.s3e: I leave when the phone already rings exactly the way you need it to.
